- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast above true trend by 1–3%.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to downward trend.
- If model shows strong upward momentum after a spike, true price often corrects; reduce forecast slope after peak by 10–20%.
- Mean reversion is stronger in low-sentiment periods; if sentiment <0.4, forecast should be capped at 1–2% below recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; use 14-day moving average as baseline for smoothing forecast deviations.
